title: Verifier‑Grounded Generate–Verify–Repair for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks: a Paired Mininet Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study to evaluate whether a verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces operationally detectable policy‑violation errors when a hosted LLM generates network configuration sequences from operator intent in a Mininet emulation. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (the same sampled initial candidate was reused for baseline and guarded pairs), N=200 paired intents were executed across three vendor‑template families and four topology patterns. Baseline success (no detected policy violation) = 196/200 (98%); guarded success = 200/200 (100%). Paired risk difference = 0.02; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.125 (predeclared primary test). An archived paired bootstrap (seed=1729, 10,000 resamples) yields a 95% percentile CI = [0.005, 0.04]; we explicitly label this bootstrap interval as descriptive/exploratory and secondary to the preregistered McNemar test. Four verifier‑triggered repairs occurred (total hosted model calls = 204), giving mean extra model calls per intent = 0.02 and mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. All numeric values, provider‑call accounting, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts are drawn from the archived evidence bundle referenced below.

sections.introduction: LLMs can assist intent→configuration translation in NetOps but produce syntax, topology, or policy errors that may have operational impact. Prior prototype work and surveys show that pairing generation with deterministic verifiers and limited repair loops (generate–verify–repair, GVR) reduces mechanically checkable errors when an adequate verifier exists [1]–[3], yet open questions remain about multi‑vendor generality and operational cost [4], [5]. We preregistered (C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1) and ran a paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to estimate whether a deterministic validator plus one permitted repair reduces per‑intent operational policy violations relative to single‑shot LLM generation. Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired design and evidence bundle under shared_initial_candidate semantics; (2) a provenance‑traced Mininet‑style emulation with 200 paired intents stratified across vendor/templates and topology patterns; (3) artifact‑grounded primary confirmatory inference (exact McNemar) and auxiliary paired bootstrap effect estimation; (4) concise reconciliation of the preregistered exact test and the archived bootstrap CI.
sections.related_work: Surveys document rapid growth in LLM‑for‑NetOps and recurring evaluation gaps (benchmark provenance, verifier integration) [5], [6]. Prototype and cross‑domain studies show LLMs can draft configurations but often introduce syntax, reachability, or semantic errors; verifier‑grounded repair and GVR architectures have been proposed and demonstrated in constrained prototypes for code and configuration‑like artifacts [2], [3], [1]. Our study instantiates a preregistered, provenance‑traced GVR evaluation at modest scale in a Mininet emulation to quantify mechanically detectable policy‑violation corrections and the model‑call cost of repairs.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: The study was preregistered (C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1) before any model calls. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (probability that an intent yields zero operationally detectable policy violations under guarded minus baseline). Design and sampling: paired binary outcomes on N=200 unique intents (baseline and guarded per intent), stratified across 3 vendor‑template families and 4 topology patterns (12 strata). Generation semantics and model: all generations used the declared model identifier gpt‑5‑mini (execution manifest: execution/model_configuration.json). The archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate: exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was produced and reused by baseline and guarded. By design, any paired outcome difference can only arise from deterministic validation and the permitted single repair call in the guarded pipeline. Validator and repair: a deterministic netops validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) checked syntax, reachability/topology constraints, and encoded policy/ACL constraints; the guarded pipeline permitted up to one verifier‑triggered repair call per intent. Execution budget and accounting: preregistered task_count=200, planned_episode_count=400, maximum_model_calls=400, initial_generation_calls_per_task=1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1. Analysis plan: preregistered primary test = exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary per‑intent success indicators; we report the paired risk difference and present a paired bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_seed=1729, 10,000 resamples) as an auxiliary descriptive interval. The archived contingency table and analysis log are available in analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl in the evidence bundle and contain the exact counts and analysis metadata used for inference.
sections.results: Execution and accounting: execution completed as preregistered (completed_episode_count=400; complete_pair_count=200). Provider audit and deterministic reconciliation record hosted_model_call_event_count = 204 (200 shared initial generation calls + 4 repair calls). Primary outcomes (archived paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 196 (both succeed), n10 = 4 (guarded succeed, baseline fail), n01 = 0 (guarded fail, baseline succeed), n00 = 0 (both fail). Baseline success rate = 196/200 = 0.98; guarded success rate = 200/200 = 1.0; paired risk difference = 0.02. Preregistered primary test: exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.125 (no rejection at α=0.05). Auxiliary estimator: archived paired bootstrap (seed=1729, 10,000 resamples) produced a 95% percentile CI for the paired risk difference = [0.005, 0.04]; we treat this CI as descriptive/exploratory and secondary to the preregistered McNemar test. Repairs and cost: four verifier‑triggered repairs were invoked (repair stage count = 4). Total model calls = 204 → mean model calls per intent = 1.02; mean extra calls per intent due to guarded repairs = 0.02; mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. Missingness and deviations: no pairs were excluded; missingness summary and deterministic reconciliation report zero failed episodes and zero exclusions. All numeric values, seeds, provider accounting, and validator traces are archived in the evidence bundle (see execution/* and analysis/* artifacts).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and reconcilement: The preregistered exact McNemar test (p = 0.125) is the confirmatory inferential result per the analysis plan; the archived bootstrap CI is an auxiliary descriptive estimate of effect magnitude. With sparse discordant counts (four discordant pairs and zero discordant in the opposite direction), resampling percentiles can produce intervals that exclude zero while an exact conditional test remains non‑significant; this is a methodological difference and not an arithmetic inconsistency. Operationally bounded implication: in an emulated setting with a deterministic validator that provides localized, actionable feedback, a small repair budget (four repairs across 200 intents) corrected all observed mechanically detectable baseline policy violations at low model‑call overhead. This does not establish production readiness or coverage of higher‑level semantic misinterpretations outside the validator's oracle. Threats to validity: (1) internal — shared_initial_candidate semantics ensure paired differences arise only from validation/repair (not from independent first‑pass generations); (2) construct — the validator covers mechanically checkable properties (syntax, reachability, ACL/policy encodings) but may miss higher‑level semantic errors; (3) external — Mininet emulation and synthetic templates limit generalization to real hardware, additional models, or alternative prompting strategies; (4) conclusion — observed baseline failure prevalence (2%) is lower than some preregistered power scenarios (the preregistration targeted a 10 pp absolute improvement and chose N=200 for margin), reducing power to detect small absolute improvements. Reproducibility pointers: archived artifacts include execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, and deterministic_reconciliation.json in the evidence bundle and supply the exact counts, seeds, and analysis metadata cited above.
sections.conclusion: We ran a preregistered paired experiment comparing single‑shot LLM generation to a verifier‑grounded GVR pipeline for intent→configuration tasks in a provenance‑traced Mininet emulation (N=200 pairs, shared_initial_candidate). The preregistered primary test (exact McNemar two‑sided) did not reject at α=0.05 (p = 0.125). Guarded GVR corrected the four observed baseline policy violations at the cost of four repair calls (mean extra calls per intent = 0.02), yielding a paired improvement of 2 percentage points (paired risk difference = 0.02). An archived paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.005, 0.04] is reported as a descriptive/exploratory effect estimate only. These artifact‑grounded results show that deterministic verifier‑guided repair can correct mechanically verifiable faults in this emulation at low model‑call cost, but they do not establish production readiness or coverage of higher‑level semantic errors; further work should expand verifier coverage, evaluate multiple models and real vendor hardware, and increase sample sizes to better power small absolute improvements. The exact contingency table and analysis log used for the primary test are archived at analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl in the evidence bundle.

disclosure_statement: Declared models/tools and provenance: declared model gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses); adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5; synthetic Mininet‑style harness and deterministic task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; after the lock the AI autonomously performed literature verification, study selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, revision, and manuscript drafting. Preregistration and artifacts: preregistration C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 preceded execution and its hash is recorded in the execution manifest; the immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Generation semantics and temperature: execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per pair reused by baseline and guarded); the archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset (null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0). Accounting and human role: preregistered task_count=200 paired intents; actual hosted model calls used = 204 (200 initial + 4 repairs); repair calls invoked = 4. No human manual editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. The evidence bundle archives execution traces, deterministic verifier traces, raw model outputs, analysis code, and manifests that substantiate reported numerical values.
limitations: Scope limited to Mininet‑style emulation with synthetic, provenance‑traced intent→configuration tasks; results do not directly generalize to production hardware or live operational environments.
Single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) evaluated; multi‑model generality is not established.

Deterministic validator coverage limited to mechanically checkable errors (syntax, reachability, ACL/policy encodings); high‑level semantic or specification misinterpretations outside the validator may remain undetected.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics imply observed paired differences derive only from validator‑triggered repair; this design does not measure effects of alternative prompting strategies or independent multi‑sample candidate selection.

Observed confirmatory effect (2 percentage points) did not reach statistical significance at α=0.05 for N=200 (exact McNemar p = 0.125); the low baseline failure prevalence (2%) reduces power to detect small absolute improvements relative to some preregistered power scenarios.
